# Extraction protocol

Weigh the frozen tissue and record the mass in the extraction log.

Add the lysis buffer and vortex the tube for thirty seconds at room temperature.

Incubate the lysate for ten minutes at fifty-six degrees Celsius.

Centrifuge the tube for five minutes and keep the clear supernatant.

Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube and discard the pellet.

Add two volumes of cold ethanol and mix the tube by inversion.

Load the mixture onto the silica column and spin for one minute.

Wash the column twice with the ethanol-based washing buffer.

Dry the column with an empty spin to remove the residual ethanol.

Elute the nucleic acids in fifty microlitres of elution buffer.

Measure the concentration with the fluorometer rather than the spectrophotometer.

Record the two-sixty over two-eighty ratio for every eluate.

Store the eluates at minus eighty degrees until the library preparation.

Label every tube with the sample barcode and the extraction date.

Report any deviation from this protocol in the laboratory notebook.
